trials.instruction: Create a NEW original, pure-Dart reusable package named aivexus_interval_union, SDK >=3.3.0 <4.0.0, with functional source at lib/interval_union.dart. Implement exactly the PUBLIC TOP-LEVEL function List<(int, int)> normalizeIntervals(List<(int, int)> input); do NOT substitute a class method for this API. Interpret every range as half-open [start,end) and reject any start >= end with ArgumentError. For valid input, return a NEW list sorted by start with touching or overlapping ranges merged. Empty input returns an empty list; a single valid range returns a fresh list. IMPORTANT DART RULES: records are immutable; never assign to record.$1 or record.$2, including last.$2, and never try to reassign final variables. To merge, construct a completely new (start,end) record and replace the appropriate element in YOUR OWN result list. Do not sort, mutate or edit the caller's input list; sort a separate COPY instead. Compute the larger end using an ordinary comparison, not an undefined max function or method. This is a functional code-generation task: write all algorithmic logic yourself rather than a stub or prewritten template. No external runtime dependencies, network, IO, shell or FFI. Return only the strict JSON source object specified by the system prompt.

Create a NEW original, pure-Dart reusable package named aivexus_delta_codec, SDK >=3.3.0 <4.0.0, code at lib/delta_codec.dart and behavioral tests under test/. Implement exactly two public functions: List<int> encodeDeltas(List<int> samples), encoding the first sample unchanged and each later entry as current minus previous; List<int> decodeDeltas(List<int> deltas), reconstructing original sample values. Return fresh lists, never mutate arguments. Empty input gives empty output; negative values must work. No external runtime dependencies, network, IO, shell or FFI. Return only the strict JSON files object specified by the system prompt.
